cards.name: Additive Dissolve (Legacy)
cards.summary: Old dissolve that adds clip B's pixel values onto clip A before fading A out, so the middle of the transition blows out hot and bright. Replaced by the newer GPU 'Additive Dissolve'.
use_for: Dreamy memory or flashback link in a documentary
Soft but energetic link between two mid-tone or darker B-roll shots in a reel (night rallies, interiors)
Glowing blend into a reveal shot; for new edits prefer the current 'Additive Dissolve', 'Flash' or 'Light Leak' transitions
avoid: Two already bright shots (snow, white kurtas, stage lights) clip to pure white mid-way
Serious news or explainer cuts: reads as stylised, not neutral
cards.equivalent: Premiere replacement: Additive Dissolve (new GPU version). AE: put B above A with blend mode Add, keyframe B opacity 0 to 100 over the first half, then fade A's opacity out over the second half.
cards.scripting: Harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 1.52-2.52 s around the 2.0 s cut (12 frames before, 13 after at 25 fps); centred needs media handles on both clips or Premiere shortens it. Probably linear like Cross Dissolve / Dip (Legacy), which were measured linear on PR 26; this one was not timed. adobe_bridge has no automatic AE version (not in XFADE/DIP): AE shows a cut unless the spec gives an ae_preset.

verified.note: Mid frame is a hot, washed-out additive mix of plate A and plate B with highlights blown toward white; the bright blend is already visible at -0.3 s.

cards.name: Band Slide
cards.summary: Horizontal bands of clip B slide in from alternate sides of the frame and interlock to cover clip A. Classic old-style Premiere slide.
use_for: Retro or deliberately cheesy segment change in a satire reel
Switching between two list items in a quick explainer
Parody of old TV-news packages
avoid: Faces: bands slice through them for most of the transition
Premium documentary or cinematic trailer: looks dated
cards.equivalent: AE: split B into horizontal strips (several duplicates with rectangle masks) and keyframe Position so odd strips enter from the left and even strips from the right; or Card Wipe with rows set and Flip Axis off as a rough stand-in.
cards.scripting: Band count and direction live in Premiere's transition settings (not settable from the spec); defaults give a handful of bands sliding horizontally. Harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 5.52-6.52 s on the 6.0 s cut; centred needs handles on both clips. Not sure whether Premiere 26 still lists it in the Effects panel or only keeps it for scripting/old projects. No automatic AE version: AE shows a cut unless an ae_preset is given.

verified.note: Horizontal bands of plate B slide in from alternating left and right edges over the static plate A, the moving B strips misaligned with each other until they interlock by +0.3 s.

cards.name: Band Wipe
cards.summary: Clip B is revealed through horizontal bands that wipe in from alternate sides while both images stay still. Like Band Slide but the picture does not move, only the reveal does.
use_for: Retro news-package or game-show parody
Quick switch between two data or chart slides in an explainer
Stylised interlude in a satire reel
avoid: Serious documentary or trailer: reads cheap and dated
Busy footage on both sides: the stripes become visual noise
cards.equivalent: AE: Venetian Blinds on A (Transition Completion 0 to 100) is the nearest one-effect match; for true alternate-side bands use strips of A with Linear Wipe at 90 and 270 degrees alternated.
cards.scripting: Band count set in transition settings, not from the spec. Harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 9.52-10.52 s on the 10.0 s cut; centred needs handles on both clips. No automatic AE version: AE shows a cut unless an ae_preset is given.

verified.note: Alternating horizontal bands reveal plate B from left and right while both pictures stay still (B lines up across bands, unlike Band Slide).

cards.name: Center Merge
cards.summary: Clip A splits into four quarters that slide and shrink into the centre of the frame, revealing clip B behind. Old CS6-era slide.
use_for: Deliberately retro or kitsch transition in a satire or meme reel
Collapsing a title card into the centre before the next shot
avoid: Any premium or serious edit: looks like a 2005 wedding DVD
Subjects off-centre get torn apart by the quarter split
cards.equivalent: Premiere: Iris Box with Reverse ticked (A closes to the centre as one box; Reverse is an Effect Controls setting, not settable from the spec) gives a cleaner result. AE: four masked quarter copies of A, each scaled to 0 toward the comp centre with Position/Scale keyframes over B.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015 (medium confidence), yet QE getVideoTransitionByName applied it fine: harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 13.52-14.52 s on the 14.0 s cut. Centred needs handles on both clips. No automatic AE version.

verified.note: Plate A shrinks toward the centre as four quarters with plate B behind; by +0.3 s only a small rectangle is left.

cards.name: Center Peel
cards.summary: Clip A tears open from the centre as four page curls peeling toward the corners, showing grey shaded curl backs and clip B underneath.
use_for: Ironic retro reveal in a satire or meme reel
Parody of old wedding or slideshow videos
avoid: The grey metallic curl backs look cheap on any serious piece
Faces in the centre are the first thing torn
cards.equivalent: Premiere: Page Peel / Page Turn for a single curl. AE: CC Page Turn on four masked quarter copies of A, each peeling toward its own corner.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015 (medium confidence); QE still applied it: harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 17.52-18.52 s on the 18.0 s cut, frames show the four grey curls. Centred needs handles on both clips. No automatic AE version.

verified.note: Plate A peels open from the centre as four curls with grey gradient backs, plate B showing through and nearly filling the frame by +0.3 s.

cards.name: Channel Map
cards.summary: Builds the transition frames from colour channels picked from clip A and clip B in a settings dialog. With the default mapping the harvest shows plain, unaltered clip A for the whole transition, then a hard cut to B at the end, so the cut lands about half the duration late.
look: channel swap only if set by hand
use_for: None from a script: at defaults it only holds clip A and cuts late; set a channel mapping by hand in the dialog if a channel-swap look is wanted
avoid: Expecting a blend between the clips: B never appears until the transition ends
Long durations: just a hold on clip A that moves the cut to the end of the transition
cards.feel: reads as a late hard cut
cards.equivalent: AE: Shift Channels or Set Channels on A, keyframed to pull channels from B (as a layer source), then cut; for a real RGB glitch use a channel-offset (e.g. Shift Channels plus Transform on separate channels).
cards.scripting: Channel choices live in a modal Channel Map Settings dialog that QE cannot set, so a scripted instance keeps the defaults (A only). Harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 21.52-22.52 s on the 22.0 s cut; frames at -0.3, 0 and +0.3 s all show clip A, unaltered (the mid frame matches clip A in the Band Wipe render to about 1/255; the colour change between frames is the source footage). Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015. Use a glitch transition instead.

verified.note: All three frames show only clip A and the mid frame is pixel-identical (mean diff about 1/255) to untouched clip A at the same instant in the Band Wipe render, so the colour change between frames is the source footage, not the transition; channel choices sit in a modal dialog QE cannot set, so a human must pick a mapping before this can be demoed.

previous.why: the harness lacked the setup it needs (see note)

cards.name: CheckerBoard
cards.summary: Clip B appears in a checkerboard pattern of squares that fill in over clip A, in two passes (alternate squares first, then the rest).
use_for: Game-show or quiz-style segment switch in a reel
Retro pixel or 8-bit themed explainer
Ironic old-TV transition in satire
avoid: Serious news or documentary: reads like a 2000s slideshow
Faces in the middle of a busy cut get chopped into squares
cards.equivalent: AE: Gradient Wipe on A (Transition Completion 0 to 100) with a precomp of tiled vertical ramps as the Gradient Layer, alternate tiles darker so one set of squares wipes first; a Generate > Checkerboard matte on B gives a cruder two-step pop. Block Dissolve is a looser random-block alternative.
cards.scripting: Square count is set in transition settings, not from the spec. Harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 25.52-26.52 s on the 26.0 s cut; centred needs handles on both clips. No automatic AE version.

verified.note: Alternate squares of plate B fill in over plate A row by row, the rest of the squares follow, and by +0.3 s only a few A squares remain at the bottom.

cards.name: Checker Wipe
cards.summary: Clip B wipes across clip A in a checkerboard of squares, each square wiping in the same direction at staggered times.
use_for: Retro grid-style transition for a quiz or list reel
Switching between two infographic slides in an explainer
Parody of old broadcast packages
avoid: Premium documentary or trailer: dated
Long durations drag; keep it short
cards.equivalent: AE: Gradient Wipe on A (Transition Completion 0 to 100) with a precomp of tiled horizontal ramps laid out as a checkerboard as the Gradient Layer, so every square wipes the same way with alternate squares offset; Card Wipe is a flipping-card alternative, not a true match.
cards.scripting: Direction and square count are in transition settings, not settable from the spec. Harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 29.52-30.52 s on the 30.0 s cut; centred needs handles on both clips. No automatic AE version.

verified.note: Squares of plate B wipe in vertically at staggered times in a checker grid over plate A, with only slivers of A left at +0.3 s.

cards.name: Cross Dissolve (Legacy)
cards.summary: The classic crossfade: clip A fades out while clip B fades in, with a linear ramp. Replaced by the newer GPU 'Cross Dissolve', which eases (smoothstep).
use_for: Passage of time between documentary scenes
Soft link between B-roll shots under VO
Single-sided fade in/out at a clip edge (fades to transparency: black only when no track below; use Dip to Black for a true black fade)
Gentle montage of archive photos
passage of time between interview answers in a documentary
softening a cut between two B-roll shots under VO
fade up from black at a clip start (single-sided)
slow emotional montage beats
avoid: Fast reels and trailers on the beat: feels slow and soft
Dissolving between two shots of the same person framed similarly looks like a mistake (use a cut or Morph Cut)
between two shots of the same framing (reads as a mistake, use Morph Cut or a punch-in)
fast reels where every cut dissolves: feels slow and amateur
cards.equivalent: Premiere replacement: Cross Dissolve (eased). AE: opacity keyframes on the top layer 100 to 0 (or B 0 to 100) over the overlap, linear for this legacy version.
cards.scripting: Linear timing (measured on PR 26). adobe_bridge builds the AE version automatically (XFADE: linear crossfade using handles). Harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 33.52-34.52 s on the 34.0 s cut (12 frames before, 13 after at 25 fps). The QE transition list contains this name twice (both entries share this card); getVideoTransitionByName returns one of them, treat them as the same. Apply by the exact name including ' (Legacy)'; centred it needs handles on both clips, single-sided it fades from / to whatever is below (black on an empty track). Prefer 'Cross Dissolve' for new edits.

verified.note: Even 50/50 crossfade of plate A and plate B at the cut, with faint B at -0.3 s and faint A at +0.3 s.

merged_from.name: Cross Dissolve (Legacy)
merged_from.summary: Older build of the standard cross dissolve: the outgoing clip fades out while the incoming clip fades in over the same frames, with a linear ramp. Kept so old projects open; the current GPU 'Cross Dissolve' does the same job with an eased ramp.
use_for: passage of time between interview answers in a documentary
softening a cut between two B-roll shots under VO
fade up from black at a clip start (single-sided)
slow emotional montage beats
avoid: between two shots of the same framing (reads as a mistake, use Morph Cut or a punch-in)
fast reels where every cut dissolves: feels slow and amateur
merged_from.equivalent: Premiere replacement: Cross Dissolve (current, eased). After Effects: overlap the layers and keyframe Opacity 100->0 on the upper (outgoing) layer, or 0->100 on the incoming layer above it, linear keyframes to match this legacy version.
merged_from.scripting: Apply by the exact name including ' (Legacy)'. The QE transition list contains this name twice (the other entry is carded in pr_transition_01); both behave the same. Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (257.52-258.52 s) with no error; gallery frames show a plain linear mix. Centred needs handles on both clips; single-sided at a clip start/end fades from/to whatever is below (black on an empty track). Prefer 'Cross Dissolve' for new edits.

verified.note: Plain even mix of A and B at the cut, B faint at -0.3 s and A faint at +0.3 s: a straight cross dissolve.

cards.name: Cross Stretch
cards.summary: Clip B stretches in from one side while clip A squashes toward the other, like a flat fake cube turn. Old CS6-era transition.
use_for: Comic squeeze between two reaction shots in a meme or satire reel
Retro side-by-side switch in a list reel
avoid: Faces get squashed thin: unflattering for politicians and anchors
Serious or cinematic edits: dated
cards.equivalent: Premiere: the newer GPU Stretch / Stretch Wipe or a 3D Spin for a real cube. AE: anchor A on its right edge and keyframe Scale X 100 to 0 while B, anchored on its left edge, goes 0 to 100; or a real cube with two 3D layers rotating 90 degrees.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015 (medium confidence); QE still applied it: harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 37.52-38.52 s on the 38.0 s cut (frames show B stretching in from the left). Centred needs handles on both clips. No automatic AE version.

verified.note: Plate B stretches in from the left while plate A squashes toward the right edge, roughly half and half at the cut.

cards.name: Cross Zoom (Legacy)
cards.summary: Clip A zooms hard into its centre, the cut happens at maximum zoom, then clip B zooms back out from close-up. No motion blur, so the midpoint is a flat blow-up of a few pixels.
use_for: Fast energetic jump between beats in a reel (keep it short)
Zooming into a detail then landing on the next shot in an explainer
Trailer impact cut when combined with a whoosh
avoid: Durations over ~0.5 s: the flat pixel blow-up at the midpoint is obvious
Low-resolution archive footage: falls apart even faster
Use the newer Cross Zoom (with blur) when available
cards.feel: hard energetic, but crude without blur
cards.equivalent: Premiere replacement: Cross Zoom (new GPU version, adds blur). AE: keyframe Scale of A up to ~400-1000% into the cut and B down from the same to 100%, with CC Radial Fast Blur or Transform shutter angle for motion blur.
cards.scripting: Zoom centre is in transition settings (defaults to frame centre). Harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 41.52-42.52 s on the 42.0 s cut; the frame at the cut is a single flat colour (extreme zoom). Centred needs handles on both clips. Zoom speed probably linear like the other (Legacy) transitions (not timed for this one). No automatic AE version.

verified.note: A is punched in hard at -0.3 s, the mid frame is a flat brown blow-up with no detail, and B is zoomed in and pulling back at +0.3 s.

cards.name: Curtain
cards.summary: Clip A splits down the middle and both halves swing open in perspective like stage curtains, revealing clip B. Old CS6-era 3D transition.
use_for: Ironic 'grand unveiling' gag in a satire reel
Opening a show segment parody with a theatrical reveal
avoid: Any serious news or documentary: looks like a 2000s slideshow
Faces in the centre are split down the middle
cards.equivalent: Premiere: Barn Doors for a flat version. AE: mask A into left and right halves as 3D layers, anchor each at its outer edge and keyframe Y Rotation 0 to about +/-90 degrees with a camera for perspective.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015 (medium confidence); QE still applied it: harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 45.52-46.52 s on the 46.0 s cut (frames show the halves swinging outward in 3D). Centred needs handles on both clips. No automatic AE version.

verified.note: Plate A splits down the middle and both halves swing open in perspective like curtains, revealing plate B, nearly gone by +0.3 s.

cards.name: Displace
cards.summary: Old CS6-era transition meant to warp one clip using the colour channels of the other. With default settings the harvest shows clip B from the start of the transition with only a faint displacement (a few pixels, invisible at normal viewing size), so it reads as a hard cut.
look: faint few-pixel warp on clip B, not visible at viewing size
use_for: None from a script; use a glitch or Liquid Distortion style transition for a warp
avoid: Expecting a displacement warp: at defaults the warp is a few pixels and reads as nothing
It moves the cut to the transition start, putting it about half the duration earlier than planned
cards.equivalent: AE: Displacement Map on A with B (or a noise layer) as the map layer, keyframe Max Horizontal/Vertical Displacement up to the cut and back down on B; or Turbulent Displace for an organic warp.
cards.scripting: Scale and wrap options are in a settings dialog QE cannot set. Harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 57.52-58.52 s on the 58.0 s cut; frames at -0.3, 0 and +0.3 s all show clip B (no clip A), so the visible switch happens at 57.52 s. B is not pristine: block-matching against the untouched source shows a spatially varying shift of about 3 px at 640 wide (about 9 px at 1080p) in nearly every block, i.e. a weak default displacement. Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015. Low confidence on what it does with other settings.

verified.note: All three frames, even 0.3 s before the cut, show clip B with no clip A, so the transition is just a hard cut at its start; scale/wrap live in a settings dialog QE cannot set, so a human must set them before a real demo.
verified.second_opinion: corrected: frames are not clean clip B; vs the untouched test_b source they differ by ~22/255 mean (clean-B controls ~4/255) and 171-179 of 180 blocks are shifted by up to ~3 px at 640 wide, so a faint default displacement warp is present on B throughout; still reads as a hard cut at the transition start, so needs_input/broken verdict kept and summary/look/scripting reworded

previous.why: the harness lacked the setup it needs (see note)

cards.name: Dither Dissolve
cards.summary: Dissolve where clip B replaces clip A through a fine, regular one-pixel dot (ordered dither) pattern, giving a grainy, screen-door blend instead of a smooth one. Old CS6-era transition.
use_for: Lo-fi or retro-computer themed explainer
Gritty archive-to-present link in a documentary
Meme or nostalgia reel with a pixel aesthetic
avoid: Heavy compression on Instagram turns the dither into mush; looks like a bad encode
Clean corporate or premium pieces: just use Cross Dissolve
Delivery below the source resolution: the one-pixel dot grid averages out into what looks like a plain dissolve
cards.equivalent: Premiere: no direct GPU replacement; Cross Dissolve for a clean blend, Mosaic or Grunge (new) for a blockier or textured break. AE: Block Dissolve on A with Block Width/Height 1-2 px and Soft Edges off, Transition Completion 0 to 100.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015 (medium confidence); QE still applied it: harvest placed the 1 s centred instance at 61.52-62.52 s on the 62.0 s cut (mid frame is a speckled blend). Centred needs handles on both clips. adobe_bridge does not map it to an AE crossfade (not in XFADE): AE shows a cut unless an ae_preset is given.

verified.note: At 640 px the mid frame is a mottled blend; in the 1080p render it is a fine regular one-pixel dot grid mixing A and B (ordered, not random), so the card wording was corrected to an ordered dither.
